author: Sooner State News
title: Former McCurtain County jail supervisor pleads guilty to federal civil rights charges
text:
Former McCurtain County jail supervisor pleads guilty to federal civil rights charges
Joseph Nelson Ebert, a former shift supervisor at the McCurtain County Jail in Idabel, Oklahoma, pleaded guilty on July 8 to one count of Conspiracy Against Rights and one count of Deprivation of Rights Under Color of Law. Each charge carries a maximum penalty of up to 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine.
According to the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma, an Information filed against Ebert on July 2 alleged that on or about September 15, 2021, he knowingly and willfully conspired with others to injure, oppress, threaten, and intimidate an arrestee in exercising their constitutional right to be free from unreasonable seizure. The filing stated this right includes freedom from unreasonable force by someone acting under color of law.
A second Information alleged that on or about January 4, 2022, while acting as shift supervisor at the jail, Ebert willfully deprived a pretrial detainee—who was restrained and not posing any threat—of liberty without due process. The document states that Ebert physically assaulted the detainee, resulting in bodily injury.
The charges stemmed from an investigation conducted by the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation and the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Magistrate Judge Gerald L. Jackson accepted Ebert’s plea and ordered completion of a presentence investigation report. Sentencing will be determined by a U.S. District Court Judge after consideration of federal guidelines; Ebert remains free on bond with conditions pending sentencing.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Nicole Paladino represented the United States in this case. The U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Oklahoma advances community wellness through federal trust responsibilities to sovereign Tribal Nations; operates facilities in Muskogee; functions under the Department of Justice; handles federal criminal investigations and prosecutions as well as civil litigation; represents the only federal judicial district fully within Indian country; and covers 26 counties including Adair and Atoka counties, according to the official website.
